name: Golden Crust Bakery
brief:
# Golden Crust Bakery — Marketing Website

## What this is
A marketing website for a neighbourhood bakery called Golden Crust. The site is
public, read-mostly, and exists to get a hungry visitor to walk in or place an
order. It must be fast on a phone, work without JavaScript for the core content,
and be trivially editable by the owner.

## Audience
- Local residents deciding where to buy bread and pastries today.
- People ordering a celebration cake or a catering box ahead of time.
- Tourists searching "bakery near me" on a phone.

## Required pages / sections
1. **Home** — hero with today's fresh-bake highlights, opening-hours badge that
   shows Open/Closed computed from the current time and the hours table, and a
   short story block.
2. **Menu** — grouped products (Breads, Pastries, Cakes, Drinks). Each item has a
   name, short description, price, and allergen tags (gluten, dairy, nuts, egg,
   vegan). Filter by dietary tag and by category, plus a text search box.
3. **Hours & Location** — a weekly table of opening hours, a holiday-closures
   list, an embedded static map image, and a "Get directions" link.
4. **Order form** — a celebration-cake / catering enquiry form: name, phone,
   email, pickup date, product, quantity, and free-text notes. Must validate the
   pickup date is at least 48 hours in the future, require either phone or email,
   and show a clear confirmation with an order reference.
5. **Contact** — phone, email, address, social links, and a short FAQ.

## Functional requirements
- Opening-hours logic must be a single source of truth reused by the Home badge
  and the Hours page (compute Open/Closed from the same table).
- The menu filter must combine category, dietary tag, and free-text query with
  AND semantics, and show a friendly empty state when nothing matches.
- The order form must reject a missing contact method, a pickup date under 48
  hours away, and a quantity below 1; on success it generates a human-readable
  order reference (e.g. GC-2026-0007) and echoes the full order back.
- Prices are shown in GBP with two decimals; totals for quantity > 1 are
  computed.
- All form validation errors are field-level and accessible (associated with the
  input, announced to screen readers).

## Non-functional requirements
- Responsive from 320px to 1440px; mobile-first.
- Core content (menu, hours, contact) readable with JS disabled.
- Semantic HTML landmarks, one h1 per page, alt text on every image.
- Colour contrast at least WCAG AA.
- No third-party trackers.

## Explicitly out of scope
- Online payment / card processing.
- User accounts or login.
- A real database or CMS backend — content is static data in the app.
- Multi-language support.

# Architecture Feasibility Study: 5-Step Process

A feasibility study in architecture is a structured evaluation that examines whether a proposed construction project can succeed given the constraints of the site, the budget, the regulatory environment, and the available technology. It typically covers site conditions, zoning codes, financial projections, design options, and risk factors.

Source: https://learnarchitecture.net/articles/31806-architecture-feasibility-study-from-concept-to-viability-in-5-steps.html

artifacts.title: Phase narrative (LLM)
artifacts.body:
**P0 — Deep Research & Feasibility:** During P0, Golden Crust Bakery's marketing website was validated as a low-complexity, read-mostly public site whose success hinges on mobile speed, no-JavaScript core content, and owner-friendly editing rather than on the architectural and engineering depth that dominates 2026 industry guidance—NCARB's AXP documentation and supervision rules, UGCE's expanded engineering feasibility requirements, and architecture-specific fee structures (time-charge, percentage of construction cost, value-based fixed/phased) all apply to licensed practice and complex construction, not to a neighbourhood bakery's brochure site. Applying the five-step architectural feasibility lens (site, budget, regulatory, functional, and scheduling constraints) in scaled-down form confirmed the concept is viable: a static-first build with progressive enhancement easily satisfies "fast on a phone," server-rendered or statically generated pages satisfy "works without JavaScript," and a lightweight CMS or markdown-based content layer keeps the site trivially editable by a non-technical owner. The remaining feasibility work is therefore not technical but editorial—defining the menu, hours, location, and ordering call-to-action that convert a hungry local visitor into a walk-in or order—so P0 concludes with a clear go decision and a narrow scope boundary.

## Mission
# Golden Crust Bakery — Marketing Website

## What this is
A marketing website for a neighbourhood bakery called Golden Crust. The site is
public, read-mostly, and exists to get a hungry visitor to walk in or place an
order. It must be fast on a phone, work without JavaScript for the core content,
and be trivially editable by the owner.

## Audience
- Local residents deciding where to buy bread and pastries today.
- People ordering a celebration cake or a catering box ahead of time.
- Tourists searching "bakery near me" on a phone.

## Required pages / sections
1. **Home** — hero with today's fresh-bake highlights, opening-hours badge that
   shows Open/Closed computed from the current time and the hours table, and a
   short story block.
2. **Menu** — grouped products (Breads, Pastries, Cakes, Drinks). Each item has a
   name, short description, price, and allergen tags (gluten, dairy, nuts, egg,
   vegan). Filter by dietary tag and by category, plus a text search box.
3. **Hours & Location** — a weekly table of opening hours, a holiday-closures
   list, an embedded static map image, and a "Get directions" link.
4. **Order form** — a celebration-cake / catering enquiry form: name, phone,
   email, pickup date, product, quantity, and free-text notes. Must validate the
   pickup date is at least 48 hours in the future, require either phone or email,
   and show a clear confirmation with an order reference.
5. **Contact** — phone, email, address, social links, and a short FAQ.

## Functional requirements
- Opening-hours logic must be a single source of truth reused by the Home badge
  and the Hours page (compute Open/Closed from the same table).
- The menu filter must combine category, dietary tag, and free-text query with
  AND semantics, and show a friendly empty state when nothing matches.
- The order form must reject a missing contact method, a pickup date under 48
  hours away, and a quantity below 1; on success it generates a human-readable
  order reference (e.g. GC-2026-0007) and echoes the full order back.
- Prices are shown in GBP with two decimals; totals for quantity > 1 are
  computed.
- All form validation errors are field-level and accessible (associated with the
  input, announced to screen readers).

## Non-functional requirements
- Responsive from 320px to 1440px; mobile-first.
- Core content (menu, hours, contact) readable with JS disabled.
- Semantic HTML landmarks, one h1 per page, alt text on every image.
- Colour contrast at least WCAG AA.
- No third-party trackers.

## Explicitly out of scope
- Online payment / card processing.
- User accounts or login.
- A real database or CMS backend — content is static data in the app.
- Multi-language support.

items.content: About half of your documented experience must be gained while employed by an architecture firm legally practicing architecture and under the supervision of an architect who is licensed in the United States or Canada—this is experience setting A. Up to 1,860 hours can be reported under Setting O, which can be performed outside an architecture ...

items.title: Engineering Feasibility Studies Requirements for 2026 - UGCE
items.content: In 2026 , engineering feasibility studies requirements go far beyond traditional cost checks and basic site reviews. With rising construction complexity, stricter regulations, and increased investor scrutiny, feasibility studies have become a strategic decision-making tool rather than a preliminary formality.

items.title: The Billable Hour Is Broken: Why Architects Are Switching to Value ...
items.content: The three main architecture fee structures in 2026 are: time-charge (hourly billing), percentage of construction cost, and value-based fixed or phased fees — each carrying different risk profiles for both practice and client. Time-charge is the default for smaller commissions and feasibility work. You log hours , multiply by rate, invoice.

items.title: 7 AXP Tips and Resources for 2026 | NCARB

items.title: Architecture Feasibility Study: 5-Step Process
items.content: A feasibility study in architecture is a structured evaluation that examines whether a proposed construction project can succeed given the constraints of the site, the budget, the regulatory environment, and the available technology. It typically covers site conditions, zoning codes, financial projections, design options, and risk factors.
